prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map places the main person roughly 0.5–1.5 m in front of the camera wearer, moving from slightly left of centre in frame 1 to extremely close and partly out of view on the right in frames 2–3, then farther away near the centre-right in frame 4 and close on the right again in frame 5. The bicycle remains behind and to the left of that person, approximately 1.5–3 m from the camera, while the paved ground recedes several metres toward the dark background. In frames 2–3, the person and a nearby hand/foreground shape occlude much of the bicycle and lower scene; frame 5 also contains a very near raised arm crossing in front of the person. Brightness makes these depth orderings clearer than the dark RGB, but the smooth gradients, merged silhouettes, and inconsistent apparent scale make precise metric distances and separations unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies the dominant person in every frame and bicycles mainly to the left or behind that person in frames 1–3; it separates overlapping person and bicycle regions that are difficult to distinguish in the dark RGB. The main person is left-of-centre in frame 1, fills the centre-right and extends beyond the top edge in frames 2–3, becomes smaller and farther ahead in frame 4, and occupies the right side in frame 5, where a foreground arm partly occludes the body. The bicycle is roughly 0.5–1.5 m behind or left of the person and about 1.5–3 m from the camera wearer when visible, whereas the person is approximately 0.5–1.5 m away; these distances come from RGB scale and overlap rather than the segmentation itself. Fragmented bicycle masks, missing body portions, changing mask colours, and several tiny “person” detections along the top of frame 4 appear unreliable, and the map does not robustly show gaze or facing direction.
descriptions.pose: The pose map supplies joint geometry absent from the dark RGB: in frame 1, the yellow body skeleton places the person ahead and slightly left, with the head above the torso, one arm extending down-left and the other down-right, and the body roughly facing the camera wearer. Small facial keypoints suggest a roughly frontal or slightly turned head, but they are insufficient to confirm eye contact; the person appears about 1 m away, with the lower arms or hands near possible mutual arm’s-reach distance. Frames 2–3 show only magenta hand skeletons near the lower centre-right, consistent with a hand very close to the camera—probably within about 0.2–0.6 m—while the rest of the nearby body is missing or occluded. No reliable pose appears in frames 4–5 despite visible people, so turning, retreat, limb reach, and the raised foreground arm in frame 5 cannot be tracked consistently from this map.
